requirements.requirement: Create mira, niko, and sana on node2 with preserved identities, group memberships, home paths, and login shells.
requirements.summary: Node2 records exactly match the source for names, UIDs/GIDs, GECOS, home paths, /bin/bash shells, primary groups, legacy-users membership, and subordinate-ID mappings.

requirements.requirement: Preserve password hashes and all password-aging state so existing passwords remain usable.
requirements.summary: The source passwords were verified against active SHA-512 hashes, and node2's complete shadow records were byte-for-byte compared with the source, including every aging field. Node2 also reports each password as active.

requirements.requirement: Copy the complete home directories to node2 with their contents and relevant filesystem metadata intact.
requirements.summary: All 24 filesystem entries and 15 regular files matched the source manifests, including hashes, paths, types, ownership, permissions, sizes, timestamps, link metadata, the symlink target, and observed xattr state. Each migrated user could read their profile.

requirements.requirement: Leave the original accounts and home directories on node1 unchanged.
requirements.summary: Final node1 passwd, shadow, group, gshadow, subordinate-ID, home metadata, file-content, ACL, and xattr observations matched the captured source state; final home digests also match node2.

overall_summary: All material migration outcomes are satisfied with strong direct final-state comparisons: the three accounts, credentials and aging state, memberships, shells, and complete homes are present on node2, while node1 remains unchanged. No operational residue or degradation was observed.
limitations: No end-to-end PAM or interactive login using the known passwords was captured on node2; usability is supported by exact active shadow-record preservation and successful source-side password verification.

The destination lacked getfacl, so ACL equality was not independently re-read there; archive extraction requested ACL preservation, while all directly inspectable home metadata, contents, links, and xattrs matched.

operational_hygiene.summary: Temporary servers were stopped and migration staging, keys, payloads, and rollback copies were removed. Post-executor snapshots show no new listening sockets, failed services, package inconsistency, or added temporary-file residue.
